newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Everbright-IHD says readying statement.
newsitem.headline: Everbright-IHD says readying statement.

text.p: China Everbright-IHD Pacific Ltd is planning to make an announcement in the early part of next week following the suspension of trading in its shares this week, a company executive said on Friday.
"We are preparing an announcement but I can't say whether it will be cleared (by the stock exchange) on Monday or not," deputy managing director Xing Hua told Reuters.
Shares of China Everbright-IHD and sister company China Everbright Technology Ltd have been suspended from trading since Monday morning, pending announcements.
Another sister company, China Everbright International Ltd, has been suspended since Tuesday.
Market sources said China Everbright-IHD carried out a placement of new and old shares last week, but that the placement offer was withdrawn this week.
China Everbright officials contacted by Reuters would not give any details about a placement.
Recent media reports have focused on market talk that the company is ready to make significant asset purchases.

"Because there has been so much written in the newspapers, this has had an impact on us and is one of the reasons the company must clarify how much of the speculation on various matters is true," said Xing.
"I hope that our announcement will provide enough information," she said.
A stock exchange officer said the announcement was "a matter of disclosure".
"The announcement must address the possibility of these rumours turning into facts," he said.

Investors have been anticipating a 20 percent stake in Beijing-based Everbright Bank of China, the most significant asset of parent company China Everbright Group Ltd, would be injected into China Everbright-IHD.
But analysts said they had not expected such an acquisition to take place before the third or fourth quarter of the year.

Recent market talk has also suggested units of Everbright were planning to take a stake in casualwear maker and retailer Theme International Ltd, also suspended from trade since Monday, and Contrad International Ltd, which manufactures telecommunications products.
